R-38…R-53 FILED. TECH-DEBT #143 + #144 + #145.** 🔴 **THE HEADLINE IS THAT `/receipts` COULD CAPTURE AND COULD NOT SHOW, AND ON 1 SEPTEMBER THAT COST EIGHT DOCUMENTS.** Lauren photographs a receipt, presses Save, the page thanks her — and that is the last anyone ever sees of it. Seventeen receipts had accumulated at LAWNS, **eight of them captured in one afternoon**, and **two produced orders while six produced nothing** — a difference that existed nowhere on any screen. **A receipt that landed and a receipt that vanished looked identical: both looked like a thank-you message.** The six reconciliation columns had been **WRITE-ONLY since 14 June** — banked at the moment of save by a wizard that then had no reader. This is that reader, plus `receipt → order → delivery` so a capture can say what it became.

**🔴 THE FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE SCREEN: THE RECON'S LOAD-BEARING FACT WAS TRUE AND MEANT THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT IT LOOKED LIKE.** The recon reported the bwi duplicate as producing orders `dc943a79` and `eb3ab2b0` — which reads as **one receipt with two orders**, and a build aimed at that shape would have rendered it wrong. Measured: **`receipts with >1 order` is 0 of 17.** It is **two receipts, one order each**, both carrying document number **19837964**, both with a delivery whose `delivery_date` is NULL. ✏️ **Same facts, different shape, and the shape is what the screen has to draw** — which is [[R-26]] arriving not as a false claim but as a true one read one level off. **And the re-measure paid a second time:** `header_amount_edited` is **false on 17 of 17** while `accept_vs_edit` reads `edited` on 17 of 17, which **narrows the open question without answering it** — whatever the owner changed before saving, **it was never the total.** The question stays David's.

**🔴 THREE PROHIBITIONS, AND EACH IS MECHANICAL RATHER THAN PROMISED — WHICH IS THE ONLY KIND THAT SURVIVES THE NEXT EDIT.** ① **NO RE-EVALUATION.** The verdict on screen is the one the owner was actually shown, not a second verdict computed today with no way to tell the two apart: `computeReconcile` is not imported **and `line_items` is not even selected**, so re-deriving it is impossible rather than discouraged. The one arithmetic is RECONSTRUCTION — `delta` was written as `lineSum − amount`, so `lineSum = amount + delta` recovers the banked figure exactly and invents nothing. ② **NO ADJUDICATION.** Six of seventeen produced no order; the row reads *"No order recorded for this receipt."* **and stops.** Not *missing*, not *orphaned*, not *an error*, and **not a blank** — an absence a reader must interpret is the defect, not the fix. **🔴 AND THE MUTANT THAT SURVIVED FIRST IS THE ONE WORTH KEEPING, BECAUSE THE BLIND SPOT GENERALISES.** Coercing an unusable number to `0` instead of to absent **broke nothing**: every *never fabricate a figure* probe had been written against `null`, which short-circuits on the first guard **before ever reaching the coercion under test.** ✏️ **The guarantee was proven for one input and assumed for the rest** — [[R-33]]'s class, and the same seam-blindness as #248's N3. The harness itself keys off the **exit code**, never a grep for the word FAIL, and asserts a **green CONTROL** first — without that, every CAUGHT could be a suite that was already red. **M1 (orders embed removed) and M2 (deliveries embed removed) both go red**, which was the prompt's own bar: a probe set that passes with either join reverted has proven neither.

### 2026-09-01 — THUNDER **THE DEPENDENCY WAS UNMET, AND CHECKING THAT WAS THE MOST VALUABLE THING I DID ALL SESSION. #250 + #251. R-36. R-37.** 🔴 **THE HEADLINE IS THAT A BUILD PROMPT ARRIVED SAYING *"do not start this until the matcher fix is owner-proven"* AND THE MATCHER FIX DID NOT EXIST.** `origin/main` was still `84cc695`, no branch matched `match`/`doc.?num`/`corrobor`, no ledger row existed, and `historyOrderWriter.ts:490` still read `if (c.differed.length === 0)` verbatim in both worktrees holding it. **Nothing was written until David ruled.** He ruled *both, matcher fix first* — two builds, two branches, in sequence. ✏️ **A precondition stated in a prompt is a claim like any other, and the cheapest possible thing to check.**

🔴 **AND THE PREMISE THE MERGED CODE RESTED ON WAS MEASURABLY FALSE.** #248's guard calls a matching document number *"an identity, not an inference."* **It is not.** LAWNS's own books — the 2026-08-29 raw capture, **1469 of 1469, `complete: true`** — carry **22 DocNumbers used by TWO DIFFERENT INVOICES EACH, 44 invoices**, every pair a different customer AND a different amount: `#3274` is Dyan Bourne at $811.88 **and** Jeffrey Gyurkovic at $4,717.50. Two defects followed, and the exposure numbers are why the dependency clause was right: **ZERO of those pairs are among the eighteen future-dated invoices the merged code runs against today, and FOUR are inside the 564-invoice import.** Both defects are **latent on `main` and go live at Stage 1**. **① `unknown` was computed and never consulted** — `corroborate()` sorts fields into agreed/differed/**unknown** and the verdict tested only `differed.length === 0`, so an existing order whose customer, date and money were all null **disagreed with nothing on earth** and got a permanent `qb_invoice_id` written onto it, after which the ordinary key skips it forever. **② Collisions were checked among OUR priors and never among INCOMING invoices** — two invoices sharing a number each returned `same-invoice` on the SAME order, the id-recording pass wrote for whichever the loop reached first, the other was logged as a benign race, **and the loser, consumed by the guard, was never planned, so its order was never created.** A real sale disappeared and loop order decided which.

🔴 **THE FINDING WORTH MORE THAN EITHER FIX: A MUTANT SURVIVED TWELVE GREEN UNIT PROBES.** Reverting the ONE line handing the new pass's result to the report — `priorOrders: settledPriors` → `priorOrders` — broke nothing. The function ran, cost nothing, and was thrown away. ✏️ **That is #248's own recorded lesson arriving one build later** (*"the unit was well tested and the seam above it was not"*, tech-debt **#134**), and it is why the fix was §M23–M30 driving `previewOrderIngest`/`commitOrderIngest` rather than a thirteenth assertion beside the twelve. **12/13 caught, 1 PROVEN equivalent** by a differential run over 10 input sets rather than asserted as equivalent, **0 real survivors.**

**Type:** Two builds, two branches, neither merged. **#250 `thunder/docnumber-matcher` (`546c16a`)** — `historyOrderWriter.ts` (`DOC_MATCH_MIN_CORROBORATION = 2`, **§②'s own settled bar reused rather than a second standard invented for one question**; new pure `refuseCompetingPriorClaims`) · `+28` assertions · `npm run verify` **exit 0 ZERO NET-NEW** (5 / 245 / 10 / 12 / 15) · **57/57 files · 2935 assertions** · `build:cultivar` exit 0. **#251 `thunder/deliveries-window`** — **NEW `lib/deliveryWindow.ts`** + 19 assertions · `DeliverySchedule.tsx` · the §9 story · **[[R-36]]** + **[[R-37]]** · `npm run verify` **exit 0, eslint 245 → 244 and the baseline RE-TAKEN to lock it** · **58/58 files · 2926 assertions** · `build:cultivar` exit 0. Both: **api/ 12/12, nothing minted · ZERO schema change · ZERO Intuit writes.** **§3 RETENTION: 1 archived verbatim (2026-08-31 (8)), 1 written — entries-in == entries-out, §3 back to 3** (archive **277 → 278**).

🔴 **AND #251 IS THERE BECAUSE THE STAGE 0 RECON WAS RIGHT ABOUT A DEFECT AND WRONG ABOUT WHICH ONE.** Recon predicted that 564 imported stops would fill an unbounded `.limit(200)` and push the nineteen future stops off `/deliveries`. True, and the lesser half. **Reading the code found `filterDate` applied CLIENT-SIDE** — `rows.filter(r => r.delivery_date === filterDate)` over that same unbounded read — so selecting **any** day outside the oldest 200 returns empty and the calendar's drill-in reports **"Nothing scheduled on this day" for a day that HAS stops.** ✏️ **Absence asserted without ever being established, on the exact surface the fulfilment tap and `openOrderNotice` mount on.** The bound now reaches the query, decided in a pure lib per **#134**; a selected day is `.eq()`'d **unclamped at any distance in the past**, and the working list is **`.or('delivery_date.is.null,…gte')`** — the `is null` half kept deliberately, because a bare floor would silently drop undated stops, which is the same defect one layer down. **Two header totals were REMOVED rather than recomputed** — both became false once the read was bounded to one day.

⚠️ **THREE THINGS I GOT WRONG AND CORRECTED, RECORDED BECAUSE THE PATTERN IS ONE THING.** **(i)** My first `npm run verify` was piped to `tail -25`, so **exit 0 was `tail`'s** and every earlier stage was discarded — a green that could not have gone red, inside the build about exactly that. Re-run capturing the real code. **(ii)** Every doc edit for #250 landed in the **main worktree on `main`** rather than on the branch; caught at `git status`, and the five files were moved by comparing **direction** (`--numstat` plus every deleted line) before restoring — #249's staged-revert lesson, applied to my own mess. **(iii)** I wrote that the calendar renders `DeliverySchedule` as its day drill-in **before checking the router** — `/deliveries` is `DeliveryRoute`; `DeliverySchedule` is mounted as a component with a `filterDate` prop, which is what exposed defect ②.

**FLAGGED FOR DAVID:** **(a)** 🔴 **#250 MUST BE OWNER-PROVEN BEFORE THE IMPORT — that is the whole reason it shipped alone.** **CARD 4c** is NEW and `needs-test` **with its reason**: it needs two invoices sharing a number AND an existing order carrying it, a state your tenant may not be in, and **an empty panel is not a pass** — provoke it in the SQL editor or leave the card red. **CARD 4b is a re-read, not a re-run: fewer of your nine may now say "will match", and that is the tightened bar rather than a failure** — each says which fields it could not compare. **(b)** ⚠️ **A DECISION THAT IS YOURS TO OVERRULE: the bar is TWO of three**, stated at `DOC_MATCH_MIN_CORROBORATION` with its reasoning. **Its effect on your nine is UNMEASURED** — it needs a read of `orders` this session did not have (the env read was denied and I did not press it). **(c)** 🔴 **CARD 16 (operations-calendar) IS WRITTEN TO BE RUN BEFORE AND AFTER THE IMPORT WITH THE SAME ANSWER.** Step 4 is the one that matters: after the import, open a **2025** day from the grid and confirm the stops are listed. **(d)** ⚠️ **THE IMPORT IS RULED, STORIED AND UNBUILT** — 564 deliveries + 564 orders + 1,565 item lines + up to **489 customer resolutions**, a table your prompt's non-negotiables never mention. **(e)** ⚠️ **`Tailgate Delivery` is deferred by ruling, but the measurement is already done so nobody re-derives it: TG and `TC` are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE across all 1,469 invoices (zero co-occurrences), TG does NOT predict shipping (40% either way), and 0 of 124 TG invoices carry `(Install & Warranty)` against 163 of 1,345 without.** **(f)** ⚠️ **#250 AND #251 BOTH INSERT A LEDGER ROW BEFORE #249 ON SEPARATE BRANCHES** — a merge conflict by construction; the resolution is *keep both* and re-take the numbers (#233). **(g)** ⚠️ **STILL OPEN AND UNTOUCHED:** the three `inventory-*` docs stamped `2026-06-13` · `docs/reference/` tracked by accident · `20260830c` and `20260831d` unapplied · tech-debt **#124**–**#127** · **#132** · **#134** · **#135**.

### 2026-09-01 — THUNDER **BOTH BRANCHES MERGED — AND THE MOST USEFUL THING BUILT WAS A TWENTY-LINE CHECK THAT WENT RED THREE TIMES AND CORRECTED ITSELF TWICE. #249. R-35. TECH-DEBT #142.** 🔴 **THE HEADLINE IS THAT THE SESSION OPENED ON A STAGED REVERT OF `main`'s HEAD COMMIT AND NEARLY MERGED ON TOP OF IT.** Eleven doc files sat staged, byte-identical to `83dc2c0` — the PARENT of HEAD — i.e. the entire #246 close-out undone: **R-32 and R-33 deleted from `RULINGS.md`**, ledger row #246 reverted, owner-test cards and `built-inventory` entries stripped. Nothing this session created it. **Merging with it staged would have folded the deletions into the merge commit, where they would read as the merge's doing.** Stopped, proven by comparing every staged blob against `83dc2c0:` and `HEAD:`, and surfaced to David, who ruled DISCARD. ✏️ **A `git status` that says `M` eleven times says nothing about DIRECTION** — the deletions were invisible until the blobs were compared against two commits, and "restore to HEAD" is only safe once you know HEAD is the good copy.

**Type:** Two merges + a build + close-out. **`thunder/fulfilled-tap` FIRST** (David's order: inventory-inert by construction, so it cannot corrupt anything while being proven), then **`thunder/history-order-lines`**. Three collisions settled AT MERGE per #233: **ledger** — both claimed #247, first-in keeps it, second renumbered **#248**; **migration** — both minted `20260831c_`, the fulfilment one became **`20260831d_`** because `20260831c_orders_qb_invoice_uidx.sql` is **APPLIED** and §6 r1 protects it (an unapplied file on an unmerged branch is being NAMED for the first time, not edited); **nine doc ledgers** — both sides kept, incoming first. ⚠️ **THE RENAME'S SECOND HALF WAS THE PART THAT NEARLY ROTTED:** a filename grep found two citations, and a BARE `20260831c` grep found **eleven more** — six of them in code comments and **one in user-facing copy on the stop card**. R-29's lesson arriving through a filename.

**🔴 THE BUILD IS A SENTENCE, AND THAT WAS THE RULING RATHER THAN A COMPROMISE.** `deliveries.status` and `orders.status` are two columns with **no code path between them** — `DeliverySchedule` writes the first and never reads the second. So a completed stop sits against an OPEN order that still HOLDS its commitment (D-52): for a checkout order with lot-anchored lines, **available is UNDERSTATED and on-hand OVERSTATED at the same time.** David ruled the tap **stays inventory-inert** — *"a control that cannot corrupt stock while being proven is worth more than one that does the whole job on day one"* — so `openOrderNotice` NAMES the divergence instead of fixing it, and the decrement gets its own build. **[[R-35]]** also rules the split-delivery clause **in advance**: one order, two trucks, one back — flip the order only when **no other unfulfilled delivery remains on it**. ⚠️ **`holdsCommitment` was EXPORTED rather than "open" re-derived** — on that comment's own standing instruction (*"promote it to an export when a real consumer appears"*), which is the first time that note has been acted on.

**🔴 AND THE FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE MERGE: A CHECK BUILT TO CATCH ONE DEFECT WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT.** The §3 retention rule has failed three times, and the root cause is structural: **each branch verifies `entries-in == entries-out` against the main it BRANCHED FROM, so the check is true on both branches and false at the merge** — nothing had ever verified it post-merge. `scripts/verify-handoff-retention.mjs` is the mechanism. **It went RED on the real tree three times**, and twice the RED was its own fault: **① it cried wolf** — two DIFFERENT 2026-06-09 sessions legitimately share a title (161 lines vs 97), so heading-comparison called real history a duplicate; **② it then MISSED the real one** — the merge had wedged the archive's own preamble INTO one copy, so the two bodies differed by four lines of boilerplate and whole-text comparison declared them distinct. ✏️ **Both failures are the same lesson from opposite sides: the thing being compared was not the thing that matters.** A check that cries wolf gets deleted, which is how the guarded thing starts failing again — so both corrections are recorded at the code as the REASONS the code is shaped that way, not as tidy final logic. **5/5 mutants on `openOrderNotice`, and M1 SURVIVED FIRST** (probe I3b passed a null id AND a null status, so the next guard returned first and the guard under test was never exercised) — **R-33's exact shape, found by mutating rather than by reading.**

**FLAGGED FOR DAVID:** **(a)** 🔴 **THE STAGED REVERT IS DISCARDED, NOT EXPLAINED — I do not know what created it.** R-32, R-33 and the #246 close-out are intact; if you staged it deliberately, say so and it can be re-applied as its own commit. **(b)** 🔴 **CARD 12 IS THE NEW TEST AND ITS SILENCES MATTER AS MUCH AS ITS SENTENCE:** a stop with no linked order must show **nothing**, and one whose order already reads Fulfilled or Cancelled must show **nothing**. **(c)** 🔴 **THE INVENTORY COMPOSITION CANNOT BE PROVEN BY ANY DATA IN THE TENANT, AND THE BOARD SAYS SO RATHER THAN LETTING A GREEN RUN STAND IN FOR IT** — the nineteen ingested stops and Saturday 08-29's six captured stops **all carry NULL lots**, so they commit nothing and decrement nothing; it needs a real **CHECKOUT** delivery order with a lot-anchored line, and none exists. **(d)** ⚠️ **`20260831d` IS STILL GATED AND UNAPPLIED** — SQL editor, not the table editor (§6 r17). **🔴 AND THE SECOND: THE PAYWALL IS PROVEN BY A SIGNATURE, NOT BY A TEST.** The requirement was that the crew screen be byte-identical with the tile off — *"prove it"*. 🔴 **AND THE DEFECT THE REWRITE SURFACED IS WORTH MORE THAN THE REWRITE: I ALMOST SHIPPED A CHECK THAT COULD NOT FIRE.** The new regex literals were written through a Python heredoc, which read every `\b` word-boundary as a **BACKSPACE escape** — so four patterns landed in the file carrying literal `0x08` bytes and **matched nothing at all**. ### 2026-08-31 (5) — THUNDER **CALENDAR: THE DAY WAS BURIED AND THE WINDOW WAS A CAGE — BOTH DISPLAY, AND NEITHER ONE WAS THE DAY VIEW. #244.** 🔴 **THE HEADLINE IS THAT THE REPORTED SYMPTOM AND THE ACTUAL DEFECT WERE DIFFERENT THINGS, AND BELIEVING THE SYMPTOM WOULD HAVE REBUILT A WORKING SCREEN.** The report was *"the day view is too small"* — David clicked a day, saw a truncated `Josh Ph…` in a cell, and concluded the drill-in was undersized. **It renders the stop, the customer, the full address, the phone, Edit customer and Route this day, and CARD 9 had already audited every affordance on it.** It was mounted **at the very bottom of the page, AFTER the "What this calendar shows" footnote**, under four weeks of grid — so a click outlined a cell and appeared to do nothing, and the ellipsis in that cell read as the entire answer. ✏️ **So the fix is scroll position, ordering and what a cell prints, and NO new day screen was built** — which is also what keeps §3-of-the-prompt's coming split (*today* and *the calendar* as two screens with two jobs) cheap instead of expensive. 🔴 **AND THE SECOND DEFECT WAS HIDING REAL WORK WHILE COUNTING IT.** The grid was fixed at *"this week and the three ahead"* with no way forward past Sep 26 and **no way back at all**, and the drill-in states the cost in its own words — *"1 stop on this day · 9 SCHEDULED IN TOTAL."* **Nine deliveries, one reachable.** Saturday 2026-08-29 — seven stops, six made, one rescheduled, the day David spent the week reconstructing — was **one day** outside it. **BUILDER-COMPLETE** `044183a`→`c435620` on `thunder/calendar-window` · `npm run verify` **exit 0 ZERO NET-NEW** (5 / 245 / 10 / 12 / 15) · **52/52 files · 2463 assertions** (+44) · **8/8 MUTANTS CAUGHT, MEASURED — M1 is the defect itself ("the window cannot move") and eight assertions fail on it** · **ZERO schema · ZERO migration · ZERO policy · no permission string** · api/ **12/12, none added** · all `[TRACE:CALENDAR]` ON.

**Type:** Fix + close-out. Code: `packages/cultivar-os/src/lib/operationsCalendar.ts` (**`offsetWeeks` · `WINDOW_STEP_WEEKS` · `weekLabel` · `windowHeading` · `cellSummary`**; `CalendarWeek` gains `relativeIndex`) · `operationsCalendar.test.ts` (**+44 probes**, §G–§I) · `pages/OperationsCalendar.tsx` (the day section moved under the grid + `dayRef` scroll-into-view · the window control · the cell). **ZERO other files touched.** Docs: ledger **#244** · tech-debt **#135** · owner-tests **CARDS 12–15 added, CARDS 1 and 9 REWRITTEN; board 15 cards · 0 covered · 14 owed · 1 needs-test** · `built-inventory.md` · `user_stories.md` (PIECES + the window clause + the landing split, filed) · ⚡ ACTIVE STATUS · DECISIONS-INDEX drift + **its `Last updated:` header corrected to a pointer, four sessions stale** · this §3 + line 3. **§3 RETENTION: 1 archived verbatim (2026-08-31, the #240 positions entry), 1 written — entries-in == entries-out, §3 back to 3** (archive **270 → 271**, counted with `grep -c '^### '`). ✅ **Own worktree** — `thunder/calendar-window`, off `main` rather than off the in-flight `thunder/workbook-reconcile`, with five other worktrees live.

**🔴 THE FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX IS THAT TWO OWNER-TEST CARDS HAD DECAYED WITH NO CODE CHANGE AT ALL.** CARDS 1 and 9 were written 2026-08-28 and asked the reader to look at **Saturday 08-29** — seven stops, and the header count of 9. The home window rolled past that date on **08-30**. So for two days both cards had been **impossible to run as written**, they still read as live instructions, and nothing anywhere watched them. ✏️ **This is [[R-26]]'s shape carrying [[R-29]]'s half-life: a card naming an absolute DATE is a claim with an expiry, exactly like a line number, and it decays on its own without anyone touching the code.** Rewritten **relative to the window**, with the absolute dates that remain marked by what makes them reachable. ⚠️ **The same rot is what made the labels wrong the moment the window moved:** the week rows were labelled by their POSITION in the grid (`wi === 0 ? 'This week'`), which is correct for exactly one window and silently calls a four-weeks-ago week *"This week"* for every other. **A label anchored to the grid describes the grid; a label anchored to TODAY describes the calendar** — so `relativeIndex` and `windowHeading` are both derived from the offset in the MODEL, and §6 r18's rule that a header is a CHECKABLE CLAIM is now enforced by a unit test rather than by a reader noticing.

**🔴 AND THE SECOND, WHICH IS ABOUT WHAT A 90px CELL CAN HONESTLY SAY.** `Josh Ph…` is a truncated name and nothing else; three of them identify nobody and read as a rendering fault rather than as a busy day. **The count is strictly more information than the names it replaces** — one stop still prints its name (a single label fits, and knowing *who* is on an otherwise empty day is the whole point of the glance), more than one prints `3 stops` · `3 stops · 1 planting` · `2 stops · all planting`. ✏️ **The planting sub-count is not decoration and was the one real design decision here:** it is the exact axis the day-type flag is about to use, so a bare *"3 stops"* would flatten the distinction the amber flag underneath is making. And a mixed-KIND day falls through to **`countPhrase`, the same function the conflict text uses** (§6 r8), so the cell and the flag physically cannot disagree about how to say *"2 maintenance jobs"* the day PMI lands.

**FLAGGED FOR DAVID:** **(a)** 🔴 **CARD 14 IS THE TEST AND THE NUMBER IS THE ASSERTION: move back four weeks, open Saturday 29 August, SEVEN STOPS, all seven listed by name.** If it is any other number, say what it is before judging anything else on the page. **🔴 THE FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE BACKFILL IS THAT TWO DEFECTS WERE IN MY OWN TOOLING, BOTH SHIPPED LAST SESSION, AND BOTH FAILED IN THE SAFE-LOOKING DIRECTION.** (1) The npm script **piped into `node`** — and when node reads a script from stdin, `process.argv` holds only `['node']`, so **no flag could ever have reached the script.** The invocation I documented, `-- --verify`, landed on the node **binary**: `node: bad option: --verify`. **🔴 AND THE SECOND, WHICH IS ABOUT LAUREN'S CATALOGUE RATHER THAN MY CODE: LAWNS SPELLS FIFTEEN PHYSICAL SIZES FORTY-SIX DIFFERENT WAYS, AND IT HAS ALREADY COST THEM A VARIETY.** `"3 gallon"` has **seven** spellings (`3gallon` · `3 gallon` · `3 gal` · `3 Gallon` · `3 Gallons` · `3G` · `3gal`); 30-gallon and 15-gallon six each. Measured against live data with the real functions: **six of 198 variety families cannot be scanned** — `detectSizeCollision` refuses, so the L5 size-picker never fires and a scan falls through to typed entry. **Five of the six are genuine duplicates and the amber flag sees them. ### 2026-08-23 (6) — THUNDER **THE LINE THAT WAS OWED THREE SESSIONS IS IN, AND IT WORKS BY CORRECTING THE WORD THAT CAUSED THE PROBLEM RATHER THAN BY SITTING NEXT TO IT.** I found this twice and refused to fix it twice, both times inside docs-only tasks, both times correctly — and it shipped in the session that was allowed to ship it. **The defect was never a missing sentence; it was that `SYSTEM_PROMPT` asked for posts that are *"warm, local, **specific**"* and supplied no facts to be specific about, which is an instruction to invent some.** So the addition reconciles that word instead of arriving beside it: ***"Specific means grounded in the facts you were given, never invented: no statistic, percentage, dollar figure, date, award, certification or comparative claim unless it appears in the supplied data. If a number would strengthen a post and you do not have one, write the sentence without it — a fabricated figure publishes under the name of the business, and the owner carries the liability."*** **ONE placement, in the SYSTEM prompt, because it governs BOTH prompts in that call** — `executeCapability('campaign_generate', {system, user})` sends them together and the user prompt is the other half that repeats *"specific"*. **RULING 1 — THE GRANT SET IS BASELINED.** Assertions 1–3 are all about SHAPE. A site can be immaculately shaped and admit a different set of people than it did yesterday, and **that is exactly what happened inside the build whose purpose was to make authority explicit.** Assertion 4 resolves every authority site — `can('literal')` bindings, inline control renders, route `permission=` props — to the ROLES that pass it, against the three bundles. A role-set change **fails the build**; the fix is to revert or re-baseline **with a `why`**. **Keyed `file::binding`, deliberately NOT `file:line`** — tech-debt #78 is that the other three caps report a false NEW on any comment edit above a tracked site, and a binding name survives the edit. **19 new probes both directions (STD-022): a narrowing fails, A WIDENING FAILS, a declared change passes, an empty grant set with no reason fails on first sight.** **STD-024 red-first against REAL HISTORY rather than a synthetic tree** — restore `CustomerCapture.tsx` at `123ad3a`, the post-Phase-2 file capA passed clean that day, and assertion 4 names it: `grant-narrowed: OWNER+MANAGER+STAFF → OWNER`.

**THE ROOT CAUSE, David's, and it is the entry's reason to exist.** When he wrote CRUD by hand, a second surface cost him time, so he built one. **For a model, generating a new component is CHEAPER than finding and reusing the existing one** — reuse requires reading and understanding what is already there first. **THE CUSTOMER FORM WAS WRITING NOTHING.** `CustomerPartyEditor` coerced each edited field against `draft` — the ON-SCREEN working copy that `input()` had already updated on the keystroke — so the unchanged-check asked *"does what I typed equal what I typed?"*, answered yes, and returned. **Fourteen of ~18 fields in edit mode silently wrote nothing, under a footer reading "Changes save automatically as you edit."** It hid because the value stays on screen until you reload, and because the four fields that DID work (Tier/Status/Credit/tax) route through `commitPatch`, which never consults the coercion — *the form looked alive because its selects were.* `CustomerEditModal` never had it: it keeps `draft` persisted and `form` working, which is how it was diagnosed. FIXED by the same split (`saved` vs `draft`), plus a skip that **snaps the input back** so the screen never shows a value the database lacks (D-9). **The TAX group folded in as an ordinary field group** — "Save exemption" removed, D-40's invariant preserved in ONE writer — which also killed a second lost-data path: a certificate number typed into a group needing a button the footer said did not exist.

**THE RULING THAT GOVERNS MORE THAN ONE SCREEN — "TRACE IS NOT A RECORD SYSTEM" (MASTER_BRIEF PART 1).** *TRACE captures a document only to EXTRACT DATA FROM IT, and passes the document THROUGH to the system that is the record.* A **receipt** is throughput to QuickBooks (`image_url` is staging, and already behaves like it). A **tax certificate** has nothing to extract and is in transit nowhere → we keep the reference and the expiry, **never the file**; the upload shell is REMOVED, **ruled out, not deferred**. **THE DEFECT.** The Roles tab wrote `role_definitions` (`upsertTenantRole`) while `has_permission`/`has_permission_for` read `business_members.permissions`, and NOTHING propagated one to the other — so "Save MANAGER" changed nothing a gate reads, and `import_pricing` was ungrantable to any manager the hour it was minted (#151's card 18, FAILED live). **THE FIX — A FUNNEL, ENFORCED AT THE DATABASE.** Two `SECURITY DEFINER search_path=''` RPCs are the only way a role→permission fact changes. `save_role_permissions` authorizes the PASSED actor as owner (D-50 scar — never `auth.uid()`, via `assert_movement_actor`), writes the tenant `role_definitions` row, **re-materializes `business_members.permissions` for every ACTIVE member of that role from the resolved role — WIPE not merge (sub-ruling #1)**, and appends the `audit_log` row (the spine's FIRST governance writer) — in ONE txn, returning per-member before/after. `assign_member_role` does the per-member case. **§1 CLOSES THE SIDE DOOR:** the `enforce_member_authority_immutability` trigger now permits a role/permissions UPDATE only under `auth.uid() IS NULL` (service/migration) OR a transaction-local GUC `trace.authority_funnel` that ONLY the funnel sets — so a direct JWT `UPDATE`, **including the owner's SQL workaround (#8)**, is refused. **Stated honestly (David's 🔴): the service-key/postgres path stays open by necessity — named, not hidden. It is a funnel for every JWT caller.** 13 write sites all route through the funnel or cease to change authority; `updateMemberRole`/`upsertTenantRole`/`deleteTenantRole` DELETED.

**BUILD 3 (screen truth) + BUILD 4 (mint/backfill).** Owner row renders every-pill-lit-and-locked from `owner_id` (BLOCKED-B answered by David's policy dump — every gated table carries an `*_owner_all` policy); the save confirm names the blast radius (who loses what) BEFORE the write; count-on-screen == member array after a save; `DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS` RETIRED, mints read the resolved floor via `resolveRoleDefaults`; the two fake pills (`apply_discount`/`override_maintenance`) hidden via the shared `UNWIRED_ACTION_PERMISSIONS`. A new permission enters the floor OFF and reaches a manager only through the funnel — import_pricing is the live grant case (card 1).

Pure `diffPermissions` test **10/0** (RED-first); `pmiInterval` **23/0** (block 3 rewritten to assert the fake pills are hidden). The migration carries V1–V8 catalog-backed checks (incl. V3 = the side-door close refuses a direct JWT UPDATE, V4 = the grant reaches the member row).

**THE DEFECT, AND WHY EVERY SCREEN LIED.** On the first live owner-prove, the plan bound the file's **Basham's** row to our **Texas Redbud** and **'Sierra'** to **Flip Side Vitex** — "Matched by item # DISC-1101/DISC-1104". The SKU-exact fast path resolved the CSV's item-# column against `business_inventory.sku`, where **`DISC-` codes are OUR internal discovery-scrape ids** (ledger #128), not the grower's namespace. Accepting would have cross-written price+attributes onto two unrelated plants. **This is the QBO-email-match (#53, nine mis-billed invoices) on a new surface — sourcing identity on a field the foreign system shares no guaranteed meaning with.**

**FIX 1 — name + size are the authority; the item # never sources.** The fast path is DELETED. Resolution is the resolver we already own and proved (`resolveCountTarget` / token equality / `detectSizeCollision`). `applyForeignId` lets the item # only **CORROBORATE** or **CONFLICT** — and per David's correction it states the **OBSERVATION** ("their item # also matches our SKU on this row"), never the conclusion ("confirms"): a coincidence between unrelated namespaces is not proof. A disagreement is surfaced red and the row defaults **unchecked**. **RULED SOFT-SURFACE (David):** name+size resolved the lot, so a namespace collision is not lot-uncertainty; hard-holding noise would train the owner to click through holds on a 116-row file. The item # is KEPT as a descriptive attribute under its own header ("Item #"), never our sku (D-24/point 3).

**FIX 2 — SIZE is folded before it is compared (David's addition, would have failed card 9).** The catalog stored sizes as bare trade numbers ("30") while CSV/child rows said "30 gal"; exact-string compare → duplicate CREATEs, and the Shoal Creek 45 CONFLICT would never fire. `normalizeSize` (already in the scrape parser) is **MOVED — not forked (STD-011)** — to the ONE shared home `utils/sizeLabel.ts` (sibling of `canonicalName`), extended to fold a bare integer to gallon-class, and reused by BOTH `sameSizeLabel` and `detectSizeCollision`. **COMPARISON-ONLY — the owner's stored value is never rewritten (D-23).** Closes tech-debt **#56**.

**PROOFS (RED-first per STD-002, both fixes).** Identity: added the two `DISC-` collision rows to the synthetic catalog (absent before — *the exact reason the green test hid the live bug: a fixture that cannot express the failure cannot catch it*) → 13 failed. Size: flipped the `countPromote.test` assertion that literally encoded the bug (`!sameSizeLabel('15','15 gal')`) → failed, then passed. ### 2026-07-22 — THUNDER ONE SELLABLE PREDICATE: the checkout picker **CAPS** instead of merely displaying the right number, and the status control **stops offering values it does not own**. BUILDER-COMPLETE; owner-prove OWED (7 cards). Zero schema, zero migration, 12/12.

**Type:** App code — **1 EDIT (the new home)** `src/lib/inventoryStates.ts` + **1 NEW test** `src/lib/sellable.test.ts` (**21/0**) + **5 EDIT** (`src/pages/ScanOrder.tsx` · `src/pages/PlantProfile.tsx` · `src/pages/BusinessInventory.tsx` · `src/components/inventory/InventoryEditor.tsx` · `src/pages/InventoryReconcile.tsx` · `src/types/plant.ts`). Docs: ledger **#147** · owner-test board (**NEW `## SURFACE: sellability`, 7 cards — 6 `owed`, 1 `needs-test`**) · `built-inventory.md` · `DECISIONS-INDEX.md` drift line · `TRACE-SESSION-BOOTSTRAP.md` ⚡ · this §3 + line 3. **§3 RETENTION: 1 archived verbatim (D-50 BUILD 2B), 1 written — entries-in == entries-out, §3 back to 3.** **NO new decision** (implements D-42/D-52/D-9). **BENCH: no trigger fires.**

**⚠️ TWO THINGS THE PROMPT ASSUMED THAT DO NOT EXIST — reported rather than invented.** The spec named "the grid 'needs-price'" and "the register" among the inline sellability sites. **Neither is a gate.** "needs-price" appears only as two COMMENTS in `InventoryCount.tsx` and as a display-only string in `CartReview.tsx:360`; the only "register" in the codebase is `tileRegistry.ts`, which is nav/tiles and unrelated. The real inline set was **FOUR** sites: the server guard in `submit.ts` (correct, kept), `PlantProfile.tsx:80` (status-only — no price, no committed), the scan review sheet (**no check at all**), and `CartReview` (display only). Saying so matters because a fabricated fifth site would have been "consolidated" into the predicate and quietly changed behavior nobody asked about.

**THE VERDICT CARRIES ITS OWN SENTENCE, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN.** `checkSellable()` returns not just *whether* but *why*, in the words the owner reads. Had it returned a bare boolean, every call site would have written its own "why not" copy — which is **precisely** how one lot came to read *"29 available"* on the picker and *"AVAILABLE 0"* on the grid. One function decides AND explains, so the reason shown is the reason applied. **Order of checks is order of USEFULNESS, not of cost:** condition → price → quantity. A DAMAGED lot holding 50 is not a quantity problem, so calling it "0 available" would be **true and useless**; it says *"Marked damaged — clear the condition in Inventory before selling it."*

**DISPLAY WAS FIXED LAST BUILD; THIS ONE FIXES THE CAP.** DISC-1105 correctly *showed* "0 available (29 on hand, 57 committed)" and **still added to the cart** — the refusal arriving five screens later at review. Now the Add button is **disabled with the reason shown**, the stepper is hidden when nothing is sellable and **greys at the cap** when something is, and the picker sub-line names the blocking reason so a pick never leads straight into a dead end. **Units already in this cart count as committed** — without that, a 10-lot scanned twice built a 20-line and waited for the server. **The server guard in `submit.ts` is untouched and stays:** a UI cap is a *courtesy* that saves five screens; it is never the authority, because a client can be stale, offline, or bypassed.

**STATUS STOPS PRETENDING.** The old list mixed two incompatible things: DERIVED (`available`/`depleted` — computed from qty per D-42) and MANUAL conditions (`damaged`/`returned`/`archived`). David proved the consequence live — he set `depleted` by hand on a lot holding 29 and it **still sold**, correctly, because the next qty write recomputes it. **A control that appears to do something and does not is a fake surface (D-9).** The dropdown now offers `available (derived from qty)` — labelled with what that row's qty actually implies — plus the three real conditions. **The derived option CLEARS a condition**, so `damaged` is not a one-way door. Both editing surfaces (grid cell + editor sheet) draw options, displayed value, and save-resolution from ONE helper, so they cannot offer different vocabularies — which is how `reserved` survived in one list after D-52 retired the concept.

**`reserved` IS GONE, AND I CHECKED BEFORE REMOVING IT.** Nothing reads `status = 'reserved'` as a condition anywhere — verified across app code, api, and SQL. The only references were a type-union member, two dropdown lists, and the SQL derive-guard `WHEN status IN ('available','depleted','reserved')`, which *permits* overwrite and therefore converts any surviving row on its next qty write. **No migration is needed**, and that is not an assumption: `status` is plain text with **NO CHECK constraint** (AC-1, stated in the migration), so narrowing the vocabulary is a UI change. **⚠️ Worth a live check anyway:** if any row currently holds `'reserved'`, it will show in the grid but sit outside the filter list until its next qty write normalizes it.

**PROOFS.** `npm run verify` exit 0, **zero net-new** (tsc 5/5 · eslint 248 · knip 10/14/15) — red first, correctly: knip flagged 1 export + 2 types as unused, all genuinely module-internal, **made private rather than re-baselined** (the D-52 `holdsCommitment` precedent, third time). `build:cultivar` exit 0. Tests **21/0** new + **55/0** existing.

**FLAGGED FOR DAVID:** **(a)** the 7 cards — sharpest are **DISC-1105 cannot be ADDED**, **a DAMAGED lot is refused everywhere and described as a CONDITION**, **DISC-1104 still sells normally** (a guard that blocks good sales is worse than the bug it fixed), and **the server refusal still fires**. **(b)** **⚠️ #66 REMAINS OPEN and is the one `needs-test` card.** The anon QR page passes `committed: 0` — **not a claim that nothing is committed, an admission that it cannot know** (`order_items` RLS is `authenticated_*`). Copy is softened to **"in stock"** (on-hand — the honest word) and the cap is at on-hand, but a fully-committed lot **will still let an anonymous customer build a cart**; the server refuses at submit, so it is a late-refusal UX gap, not an oversell hole. **PROPOSED, NOT BUILT** (it is a migration and this build ships none): `SECURITY DEFINER public.lot_available(uuid) RETURNS int`, GRANTed to `anon`, returning **only the derived integer** — no order rows, no customer data — closing #66 without widening `order_items` RLS and without a new api function. **Your call.** **(c)** the live `'reserved'` row check above. **(d)** #67 (blind capture) still your open build input; #56/#59/#60/#61/#62/#63/#64/#65/#68/#69/#70 unchanged.

### 2026-07-22 — THUNDER 2B DEFECT FIX: the reconcile replay counted a **POSITION** as a **MOVEMENT**. **The reported diagnosis was wrong, and saying so is the point of this entry.** Also: the checkout picker showed on-hand wearing the word "available". BUILDER-COMPLETE; owner-prove OWED (2 cards). Zero schema, zero migration, 12/12.

**Type:** App code — **3 EDIT** (`src/lib/reconcileMath.ts` · `src/lib/reconcileMath.test.ts` **55/0, 7 new** · `src/pages/ScanOrder.tsx`). Docs: ledger **#146** · owner-test board (**2 NEW cards** under `## SURFACE: reconcile`) · `tech-debt-log.md` **#70 NEW** · `DECISIONS-INDEX.md` drift line · `TRACE-SESSION-BOOTSTRAP.md` ⚡ · this §3 + line 3. **§3 RETENTION: 1 archived verbatim (D-50 LAYER 2A-2), 1 written — entries-in == entries-out, §3 back to 3.** **NO new decision.** **BENCH: no trigger fires.**

**⚠️ THE HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG, AND THE REAL CAUSE IS MORE INTERESTING.** The prompt's diagnosis — *"the replay sums BOTH the raw table AND the D-51 read-view, so every row is counted once from each source"* — is **not what is happening.** There is exactly **ONE** read, of `business_inventory_ledger`, at `InventoryReconcile.tsx:182`; no view, no union, no join. Reported as instructed rather than forced to fit.

**The actual cause:** the D-50 **genesis backfill dates every `opening_balance` at `now()`** — `20260720_inventory_movement_ledger.sql:360`, i.e. **migration-apply time (2026-07-20), not the lot's origin.** So for any lot last counted BEFORE that date, the genesis row falls **inside** the since-that-count window and is replayed as if the stock had just arrived: `prior 60 + genesis 60 = 120` against a book of 60. **It reads as a clean 2× only because genesis `delta = bi.qty` = current on-hand, which on a lot untouched since its last count IS `prior.counted_qty`.** Two different numbers that happen to be equal — which is precisely how a doubling *illusion* gets manufactured out of a single read, and why "exact doubling ⇒ read twice" was such a reasonable inference. The numbers reconcile exactly: true replay **58** (opening +60, count_reconcile −2), and **120** is `60 + 60`, not `2 × 60`.

**THE FIX IS A DISTINCTION, NOT A DATE PATCH.** `isMovement()` now lives in the PURE module: an `opening_balance` **asserts a position** ("this lot stood at N when the ledger adopted it"); it does not **record a change**. Replaying a position on top of a count that already reflects it adds the entire stock twice. The filter is applied **once**, feeding BOTH the arithmetic and the evidence strip — so the number the owner is asked to explain and the movements shown as its explanation can never disagree (STD-011). **Correct in every case, not just for the synthetic date:** a genesis row older than the window is already date-excluded, and a lot born after adoption gets a ZERO-delta `opening_balance` (`:798`; a promoted lot with real stock is written as `count_reconcile`, `:584`). It never discards a real quantity.

**MUTATION-PROVEN, against the live numbers.** Reverting the filter reproduces the reported figures exactly — replay 120 vs book 60, and the 58 case — failing 5 assertions. The regression test is written from David's own SQL (lot `3ec53db3`, 2 rows, SUM 58), so the check is against the database's answer, not mine.

**SECOND FIX — SAME CLASS, WHICH IS WHY IT SHIPPED HERE.** `ScanOrder.tsx:237,275` read raw `row.qty` and labelled it **"available"**: DISC-1105 printed *"29 available"* while `/inventory` showed **AVAILABLE 0** (29 on hand, 57 committed). Both sites now route through the SAME D-52 derivation the grid and the oversell guard use (`availableFrom` over `fetchCommittedByLot`) — one definition, no drift. **Both numbers are named when units are committed** (*"0 available (29 on hand, 57 committed)"*), for the same reason D-52's refusal copy does: a bare "0 available" against a lot the owner can see holding 29 reads as a bug, not a rule. **A picker that offers stock the server will refuse teaches the owner to distrust the refusal, not the picker.**

**⚠️ A THIRD SITE WAS FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED.** The grep turned up `PlantProfile.tsx:52` — the **anonymous QR page** — also printing `{c.qty} available`. That is **tech-debt #66**, and it is structural: `order_items` RLS is `authenticated_*`, so an anon customer **cannot derive committed**. Applying the same fix would silently return `committed = 0` and render the **identical wrong number while looking corrected** — worse than leaving it, because it would retire the debt without paying it. Still David's call (server-side derived read, minding 12/12 · or soften the copy to "in stock").

**PROOFS.** `npm run verify` exit 0, **zero net-new** (tsc 5/5 · eslint 248 · knip 10/14/15). `build:cultivar` exit 0. Tests **55/0**.

**FLAGGED FOR DAVID:** **(a)** the 2 cards — lot `3ec53db3` must replay to **58** with the mismatch line ABSENT; the DISC-1105 picker must read **0 available (29 on hand, 57 committed)**. **(b)** **#70 NEW** — the genesis rows' synthetic `occurred_at` is fixed at the consumer, but the hazard stays in the DATA for the next time-windowed reader. Re-dating them is **rejected outright**: that is an UPDATE on an append-only table whose trigger rejects it even for `postgres`, and we do not break that guarantee to tidy a timestamp. **(c)** your WRITE-path read was right — one `count_reconcile`, delta −2, qty→58, `SUM(delta)=58`; only the replay DERIVATION was wrong, and baseline mode was never affected. **(d)** #66 above. **(e)** #67 (blind capture) still your open build input; #56/#59/#60/#61/#62/#63/#64/#65/#68/#69 unchanged.

### 2026-07-21 — THUNDER D-50 BUILD 2B: the RECONCILE SCREEN — a physical count becomes STAMPED, DATED, ATTRIBUTED truth on the append-only ledger. **The spec's two central formulas were both wrong; both were corrected and the corrections are mutation-proven.** BUILDER-COMPLETE; owner-prove OWED (9 cards). Zero api-fn (12/12), zero schema, zero migration.

**Type:** App code — **2 NEW** (`packages/cultivar-os/src/pages/InventoryReconcile.tsx` · `src/lib/reconcileMath.ts` — the PURE decision) + **1 NEW test** (`src/lib/reconcileMath.test.ts`, **48/0**) + **3 EDIT** (`src/router.tsx` · `src/registry/tileRegistry.ts` · `src/pages/BusinessInventory.tsx`). Docs: ledger **#145** · `built-inventory.md` (line 4 + NEW capability entry) · owner-test board (**NEW `## SURFACE: reconcile`, 9 cards all `owed`**) · `tech-debt-log.md` **#67 + #68 + #69 NEW** · `DECISIONS-INDEX.md` drift line · `TRACE-SESSION-BOOTSTRAP.md` ⚡ · this §3 + line 3. **§3 RETENTION: 1 archived verbatim (OWNER-GATED DEV SURFACES), 1 written — entries-in == entries-out, §3 back to 3.** **NO new decision** (implements D-50; **R-STATUS and blind-capture deliberately left OPEN**). **BENCH: no trigger fires** (no payments/PII-export/webhooks/AI-calls/compliance-actions — roster matched, reported per §6 r10). **§1.6:** applicable — **1 STORY** ("Reconcile the count against the ledger — leakage becomes arithmetic", ARC asset-inventory-pmi, MAPS-TO 2.3/5.1 — cited; its BUILD INPUT (1) *"where the real actor comes from"* is ANSWERED here (the signed-in desk user), BUILD INPUT (2) *blind capture* is NOT and stays David's), **3 VALIDATION** (negative/fractional counts and zero-qty attributions refused **before** the RPC; the over-attribution refusal NAMES the number it refused against), **4 CRUD-PERMISSIONS** (VIEW_COSTS route gate + `assert_movement_actor` server-side — defence in depth, not one lock), **6 AC-1/3** (no vertical noun; tenant scope untouched), **7 FUNCTION THRIFT** (zero api-fn — RPCs are postgres functions, reads run under existing RLS), **8 REUSE** (reserved/available through the ONE D-52 derivation, imported never re-exported), **9 TRACE STAYS ON** (`[TRACE:RECONCILE]` ON by birth), **11 OWNER-TEST** (9 cards, `owed`).

**⚠️ THE HEADLINE: BOTH OF THE SPEC'S FORMULAS WOULD HAVE WRITTEN FALSE ROWS INTO A LOG THAT CANNOT BE RETRACTED.** **(A) `expected` is a FULL REPLAY, not `prior_count − sales`.** The ledger records every movement — receive · dead · loss · found · adjust · tombstone — not only sales. Subtracting sales alone makes any non-sale movement in the window surface as a residual: a **+10 receive becomes a −10 gap the owner is asked to explain as shrinkage that never happened.** That is D-9 *inverted* — it mis-attributes a REAL movement rather than fabricating one — and it asks a human to account, permanently and by name, for the system's own arithmetic error. **(B) Attribution SPLITS the delta; it does not add a second one.** `count_reconcile_inventory` and `adjust_inventory_manual` **both move qty**. Run in the specified sequence — count_reconcile for the whole change, *then* a dead/loss adjust per cause — they decrement **twice**: book 30, counted 13, attributed 4 dead + 3 lost lands on-hand at **6**, net **−24 instead of −17**. *Seven invented dead plants, unretractable.* Each cause now writes its own qty-moving event and the **unexplained remainder** lands on the closing `count_reconcile`, so the steps sum to exactly `counted − book` and every cause gets the permanent dated line D-50's story literally asks for ("4 dead, 3 unexplained loss"). **Neither correction is a judgement call — each is proven by MUTATION TEST: reverting the code to the spec's version fails the suite (2 tests for A, 6 for B).**

**THE DECISION IS PURE, AND THAT IS THE ARCHITECTURE, NOT A PREFERENCE.** `reconcileMath.ts` performs no IO — mode detection, replay, residual, variance, and the ordered write PLAN are all functions of their inputs, and the page only executes what they return. Extracted pure for the same reason `countPromote.ts` was at D-49: **arithmetic that decides what enters an append-only log must be testable without a database, because a wrong row can only be apologized for with a second row.** Order inside the plan is load-bearing twice: **credits before debits** (a −6 dead before a +4 found on a lot of 3 would RAISE at the RPC and **strand half an attribution permanently**, with no way to finish it), and the **closing step lands ABSOLUTELY on `counted`** so a sale landing mid-plan is absorbed into that one row rather than silently lost. `miscount` is deliberately NOT an attribution kind — "the book was wrong, nothing physically happened" is *exactly* what a `count_reconcile` row already means, so it is the REMAINDER; giving it its own event would assert a movement that did not occur.

**BASELINE HIDES THE COLUMN RATHER THAN EMPTYING IT.** On a fresh tenant every lot is BASELINE and the "Since last count" column **does not exist** — not rendered blank. An empty sold-column on the screen built to prove how easy this is invites "why is this blank?", which is the opposite of the demo's point. It appears automatically the moment any lot has a window. Same reasoning made baseline ask for **no attribution**: there is no history to explain a first count against, so demanding one would be theatre.

**THE QUALITY GATE CAUGHT A REAL GAP I HAD NOT CONSIDERED.** `verify-universals` cap **#r** failed the first run: *"routes reachable but with NO nav entry (URL-only/orphaned): /inventory/reconcile."* The cheap fix was adding it to the EXCEPTIONS list beside `/inventory/count`. That would have been wrong — count is a sub-flow entered mid-task, but **reconcile is a destination the owner goes to deliberately**. It got a real `NAV_IA` node under Inventory, plus a "Reconcile count" button beside "Start count" on the grid. *"A new surface cannot ship without nav"* did its job.

**PROOFS.** `npm run verify` **exit 0, zero net-new** (tsc 5/5 · eslint 248 · knip 10/14/15) — and it went red first, correctly, three times: knip flagged 4 unused exports + 3 unused types in `reconcileMath.ts` (all genuinely module-internal — made private, **not re-baselined**, per the D-52 `holdsCommitment` precedent), eslint caught a floating promise and an async `onClick`, and `#r` caught the orphan route. `build:cultivar` exit 0. Tests **48/0**. Self-caught while writing the Accept sheet: Reserved was derived as `book − available`, which **understates it whenever committed exceeds on-hand** (`availableFrom` floors at 0) — reserved is a read fact, not a subtraction, so it is now passed in.

**FLAGGED FOR DAVID:** **(a)** **⚠️ #67 — BLIND CAPTURE IS THE MISSING HALF AND IT IS YOUR OPEN BUILD INPUT.** `InventoryCount.tsx:438` already calls `count_reconcile_inventory` **at capture**, so a phone count applies itself and a desk reconcile *of that walk* reads residual **0 by construction**. DELTA mode is real and provable for movements landing **after** a count (which is what owner-prove step 2 exercises), but it is **not** the count-then-review loop the story describes. `blind_capture_mode` is named in that story's own `PIECES:` — **does it ship, and is it default-blind?** **(b)** the 9 cards; sharpest are the **RECEIVE** card (a non-sale movement must read residual **0**, never phantom shrinkage) and the **ATTRIBUTION-SPLIT** card (read the "What Accept writes" box *before* confirming: 3 steps, ending on **13**, `SUM(delta) = −17` not −24). Then re-run LAYER 1's **V3(b)** — `qty == SUM(delta)`, 0 rows, with the new reconcile events in the sum. **(c)** **#68 NEW** — session scoping is **not built**, and the spec asked for it: blocked by #67, and `inventory_count_sessions.status` already has one owner (a second writer is the STD-011 drift we keep paying for). **(d)** **#69 NEW** — a multi-step accept can **partially land** (the sequence is not atomic even though each RPC is); mitigated by an honest stop-message naming the step and by the absolute closing step, durable fix is a one-RPC plan = a migration. **(e)** the `was_unknown` queue **READS but offers no Resolve button** — deliberate: a control that looks actionable and isn't is a dead affordance, and the card says so. **(f)** #56/#59/#60/#61/#62/#63/#64/#65/#66 unchanged.

### 2026-07-21 — THUNDER D-52: the THREE-NUMBER inventory model lands in CODE — on-hand stops moving at checkout and starts moving at FULFILLMENT. **The spec named 2 seams; there were 4, and the other 2 would have INVENTED stock.** BUILDER-COMPLETE; owner-prove OWED (8 cards); remediation REPORT-ONLY pending David's confirm. Zero api-fn (12/12), zero schema, zero migration.

**Type:** App code — **1 NEW** (`packages/cultivar-os/src/lib/inventoryStates.ts` — THE derivation home) + **1 NEW script** (`scripts/d52-remediate-committed-stock.mjs`) + **4 EDIT** (`api/orders/submit.ts` · `api/dashboard.ts` · `src/pages/BusinessInventory.tsx` · `src/pages/Dashboard.tsx`). Docs: ledger **#144** · `built-inventory.md` (line 4 + the D-42 entry marked SUPERSEDED-IN-PART) · owner-test board (**NEW `## SURFACE: inventory-states`, 8 cards all `owed`** + the D-50 checkout-sale card **amended** — it now says "run this as a WALK-IN only") · `tech-debt-log.md` **#65 + #66 NEW** · `DECISIONS-INDEX.md` (D-52 row flipped from DOCS-ONLY to BUILT + drift line) · `TRACE-SESSION-BOOTSTRAP.md` ⚡ · this §3 + line 3. **§3 RETENTION: 1 archived verbatim (SHA STAMP), 1 written — entries-in == entries-out, §3 back to 3.** **NO new decision** (implements D-52; **R-STATUS deliberately left OPEN**). **BENCH: no trigger fires** (no payments/PII-export/webhooks/AI-calls/compliance-actions — roster matched, reported per §6 r10). **§1.6:** applicable — **1 STORY** (D-52's, cited), **3 VALIDATION** (the refusal names both numbers, never a bare "0 in stock" against a lot the owner can see holding 12), **4 CRUD-PERMISSIONS** (unchanged — `handleStatus` remains manager-gated), **6 AC-1/3** (no vertical noun; tenant scope untouched), **7 FUNCTION THRIFT** (zero api-fn), **8 REUSE** (ONE derivation read by the checkout guard AND the grid AND the dashboard), **9 TRACE STAYS ON** (`[TRACE:INVENTORY]` ON by birth on every new branch), **11 OWNER-TEST** (8 cards, `owed`).

**⚠️ THE HEADLINE: THE SPEC NAMED TWO SEAMS. THERE WERE FOUR — AND THE UNNAMED TWO WOULD HAVE MANUFACTURED PLANTS.** BUILD 1 correctly identified the checkout decrement and the missing `fulfilled` branch. But **four** call sites touch on-hand on the order path, and the other three — the **cancel-restore**, the **delete-restore**, and `handleUpdate`'s **edit-delta arithmetic** — were every one of them written believing *checkout had already decremented*. That belief was true under D-42 and became false the instant the decrement moved. Left alone, **cancelling a pending order would have credited stock back for a decrement that never happened** — inventing plants the nursery does not have, and D-50's append-only ledger would have recorded the invention as unretractable fact. The same for deleting an open order, and the edit path would have drifted on-hand by (old − new) on orders that never took anything. **All four now key off ONE predicate — `movesOnHand(status)` — so there is a single answer to "did this order's stock physically move?" instead of four sites each assuming it.** That consolidation *is* the fix; moving the decrement was the easy half.

**⚠️ THE REMEDIATION EXCLUDES WALK-INS, AND THE SPEC DID NOT SAY TO.** BUILD 5 said: for each unfulfilled order line, credit +qty back. Applied literally that **over-credits every self-transport order still sitting `pending`** — those customers paid and drove away with the plants the same day. The stock is genuinely gone; D-42 decremented it **correctly**; the status reads `pending` only because no transition UI ever existed to close it. Crediting them would invent stock in a log that cannot be retracted — the exact failure D-50's immutability exists to prevent, committed by our own hand. **The script therefore splits by `transport_method` and reports all three buckets (remediate · skipped-walk-in · skipped-no-lot) so David checks the judgement rather than trusting it.** It is **REPORT-ONLY by default**; `--apply` is opt-in and writes LEDGERED events (`kind='d42_remediation'`, `p_reason` naming the order), never a silent UPDATE. **I could not run the report myself — the sandbox blocks reading `.env` files, which is correct for secrets — so the 16-order list is David's to produce and confirm.** That constraint pushed the deliverable into the shape it should have had anyway: a gated script, like the migration.

**COMMITTED IS DERIVED, AND THAT WAS ONE OF D-52'S TWO OPEN BUILD INPUTS.** No column was added. `committed` = SUM of open order-line quantities; `available` = on-hand − committed. A stored `committed` would be a **second representation of the open orders** and would drift from them (STD-011) — the orders ARE the commitment, so we read them. `holdsCommitment` is derived **by exclusion** (not `fulfilled`, not `cancelled`) rather than an allow-list, deliberately: **R-STATUS is still open**, and a new *open* state is likelier than a new terminal one — so an unratified future status defaults to **holding** its commitment (stock protected) instead of silently releasing it (stock oversold). **Fail toward not overselling.** Same reasoning made the walk-in's status load-bearing: it is born `fulfilled`, because leaving it `pending` would count units as committed that are already on a customer's trailer.

**THE CARD THAT JUSTIFIES THE BUILD.** Two delivery orders for the same units: the second is now **refused against AVAILABLE while the grid still shows the stock on hand**. Under D-42 that second order **succeeded** — selling the same physical plants twice. The refusal message names both numbers on purpose (*"Only 0 available to sell (12 on hand, 12 committed to open orders)"*), because a bare *"only 0 in stock"* against a lot the owner can see holding twelve reads as a bug, not a rule.

**PROOFS.** `npm run verify` **exit 0, zero net-new** (tsc 5/5 · eslint 248 · knip 10/14/15) — and it went red first: knip flagged `holdsCommitment` as an unused export, which was **correct** (nothing outside the module consumes it), so it was made internal rather than re-baselined. `build:cultivar` exit 0. **⚠️ The gate is BLIND to the two `api/` files this build edits** (`tsconfig.json` → `include: ["src"]`), so `submit.ts` + `dashboard.ts` were typechecked **directly** under `--strict` → **exit 0**; *that* is the type evidence, not the green gate. Now recorded as **tech-debt #65** rather than re-flagged each build.

**FLAGGED FOR DAVID:** **(a)** run the **remediation REPORT** and confirm the two lists — especially that every "SKIPPED: walk-in" row is genuinely a customer who drove away. Nothing writes until you say so. **(b)** the 8 cards; sharpest are the **oversell-against-available** card and **"Cancelling an OPEN order invents no stock."** Then re-run Layer 1's **V3(b)** — `qty == SUM(delta)` must still be 0 rows *with the remediation events in the sum*. **(c)** **tech-debt #66 NEW** — the anonymous QR plant page still shows ON-HAND under the word "available", and **structurally cannot** show otherwise: `order_items` RLS is `authenticated_*` by policy (verified by reading it), so an anon customer cannot derive committed. The server refuses correctly, so it is a UX gap, not an oversell hole — **your call between a server-side derived read (mind §6 r11, 12/12) and simply softening the copy to "in stock"**, which is nearly free. **(d)** **tech-debt #65 NEW** — the quality gate cannot see `api/`. **(e)** **R-STATUS is still OPEN** — this build deliberately did not ratify it, and #64 (`qbo/.../cultivar.ts` writing an undeclared `invoiced`) still means an order can reach a state that emits no lifecycle event. **(f)** #56/#59/#60/#61/#62/#63 unchanged.

### 2026-07-20 — THUNDER D-50 LAYER 2A-2: the ORDER PATH now writes to the ledger — lifecycle transitions AND the sale, one append-only event stream. **The spec's central premise was FALSE and was corrected, not built to.** BUILDER-COMPLETE; migration GATED; owner-prove OWED (6 cards). Zero api-fn (12/12).

**Type:** App code + schema — **1 NEW migration** (`supabase/migrations/20260720_ledger_event_store_columns.sql` — GATED, David applies) + **1 EDIT** (`packages/cultivar-os/api/orders/submit.ts`). Docs: ledger #143 · `built-inventory.md` line 4 · owner-test board (**NEW `## SURFACE: order-events`, 6 cards, all `owed`**) · `tech-debt-log.md` **#64 NEW** · `DECISIONS-INDEX.md` drift line · `TRACE-SESSION-BOOTSTRAP.md` ⚡ · this §3 + line 3. **§3 RETENTION: 1 archived verbatim (D-50 Layer 1), 1 written — entries-in == entries-out, §3 back to 3.** **NO new decision** (implements D-50; deliberately does NOT ratify R-STATUS). **BENCH: no trigger fires** (no payments/PII-export/webhooks/AI-calls/compliance-actions — roster matched, reported per §6 r10). **§1.6:** applicable — **1 STORY** (D-50's, cited; the CONFLICT clause fired — see below), **6 AC-1/2/3** (no vertical noun; tenant scope unchanged; the view inherits base-table RLS and widens nothing), **7 FUNCTION THRIFT** (zero api-fn — RPCs are postgres functions), **8 REUSE** (one order-event seam; the aggregate defaults live in the ONE emit function so all six LAYER 1 RPCs inherit them **unedited**), **9 TRACE STAYS ON** (`[TRACE:INVENTORY]`/`[TRACE:ROSTER]` ON by birth), **11 OWNER-TEST** (6 cards, `owed`).

**⚠️ THE SPEC WAS BUILT ON A STATUS THAT DOES NOT EXIST — AND THAT IS THE HEADLINE.** BUILD 3 specified: *"the PAID transition ALSO writes the stock SALE event."* There is **no `paid` status**. `ORDER_STATUSES` is `pending | confirmed | fulfilled | cancelled` (`orderStatus.ts:13`) — the spec named THREE statuses that do not exist (`created`, `paid`, `delivered`). Worse: **no status transition decrements stock at all.** The decrement lives in `handleCreate` §11, at **CHECKOUT**, where the order is born `pending`. So the specified build was unbuildable and its owner-prove step (*"David marks an order PAID through the app"*) was unperformable. **Where the false premise came from is the lesson:** the decrement block's own comment called itself *"the ORDER-PAID/CONFIRMED commitment point … the stock is committed here, at payment."* **A comment describing a payment lifecycle the code does not have** — read in good faith, it sent a build spec hunting a transition that was never there. **That comment is now corrected in place** (tech-debt **#61**'s exact class: a comment contradicting its own repo costs real reasoning). Per the **§9 story-reconciliation gate** — *CONFLICT → STOP, surface, resolve before building* — this went to David rather than being resolved by inventing statuses, which would have silently ratified **R-STATUS**, an OPEN decision `orderStatus.ts:7-8` explicitly reserves for him. **David ruled: build to the real four, date the sale at checkout, leave R-STATUS open.**

**⚠️ THE BACKFILL WAS REFUSED, AND REFUSING IT IS THE BUILD'S BEST DECISION.** The spec asked for one `UPDATE` setting `event_type = kind` on the 131 existing rows — *"additive."* It is not additive; it is an amendment of history. `business_inventory_ledger` carries a trigger that rejects UPDATE/DELETE **even for `postgres`** — owner-proven V2 on 2026-07-20, and called out AT THE TIME as the whole point, *because it defends against our own future code*. The backfill would have required `ALTER TABLE … DISABLE TRIGGER`: **the ledger's first extension would have opened the exact door the ledger exists to weld shut.** And it was never needed — `event_type` IS `kind`, `aggregate_type` IS `'INVENTORY'`, `aggregate_id` IS `inventory_id` for every historical row, so storing them is a **second copy of one fact (STD-011)**. A read-view (`business_inventory_ledger_events`) resolves them with zero mutation, and **card V2 now PROVES no historical row was rewritten** (`untouched == total`). The guarantee survived its own first upgrade — which is the thing worth testing.

**WHAT SHIPPED.** Three nullable columns + an aggregate index + the read-view. `emit_inventory_movement` widened 9→12 args (**DROP-then-CREATE, not overload** — the LAYER 1 §7a trap: a second overload makes every existing 9-arg call AMBIGUOUS and they all start failing); the new params DEFAULT to `'INVENTORY'` + `inventory_id`, **so all six LAYER 1 RPCs populate the aggregate columns correctly with zero edits to any of them.** New `record_order_event` — **`delta` is hard-coded 0 inside the RPC, not a parameter**, because an order event must never be able to move on-hand and making that un-passable beats trusting every future caller. Granted **service_role only**, deliberately NOT `authenticated`: `assert_movement_actor` stops a client forging someone else's id, but a signed-in manager with EXECUTE could still write arbitrary lifecycle events into a log nobody can retract. In `submit.ts`, all **4** `adjustLotQty` sites now carry actor + `kind` + `occurred_at` + `source_id=order`, and **4** order events emit (`order_created` · `order_edited` · `order_deleted` · `order_${status}`). The transition event is **derived** (`order_${status}`), not a hand-maintained switch — when David ratifies R-STATUS the new statuses emit for free; a switch would silently miss them.

**THE NULL ACTOR IS A FEATURE AND THE CARD SAYS SO.** The spec said *"thread the real caller, do not pass null."* Half right. `handleCreate` is **anon-createable** — the customer QR checkout has no caller — and `assert_movement_actor` explicitly admits a NULL actor as an honest system write, with D-50 §11 stating it must **never** be defaulted to the owner. So the actor is threaded wherever one exists (edit/delete/cancel/status, all manager-gated) and stays **NULL on anonymous checkout**. The owner-test card asserts that NULL is a **PASS** and that recording the owner's uid there is the **FAIL** — a fabricated actor is worse than an absent one (D-9).

**⚠️ `npm run verify` IS BLIND TO THE FILE THIS BUILD EDITS.** The gate passed **zero net-new** (tsc 5/5 · eslint 248 · knip 10/14/15) — but `packages/cultivar-os/tsconfig.json` has `include: ["src"]`, so **`api/` is never typechecked** and the green gate says nothing about `submit.ts`. Confirmed by `tsc --listFiles | grep -c submit` → **0**. `submit.ts` was therefore typechecked **directly** under `--strict` (exit 0), and *that* is the evidence — not the gate. `build:cultivar` exit 0. **Flagged as a real hole:** the deployed backend is exactly the surface the quality gate cannot see.

**FLAGGED FOR DAVID:** **(a)** **apply the migration** — every card fails honestly until then. **(b)** the 6 cards; sharpest are **V2** (`untouched == total`) and the **anonymous-NULL-actor PASS** card. Then re-run Layer 1's **V3(b)** — `qty == SUM(delta)` must still be 0 rows under the new writers. **(c)** tech-debt **#64 NEW** — `qbo/invoice/cultivar.ts:658` writes `status: 'invoiced'`, a value `ORDER_STATUSES` does not contain and `handleStatus` would reject; **flag-only per your ruling**, but note an order can now reach a state that emits **no** lifecycle event. **(d)** **Layer 2 for the COUNT path is still owed** — this build did the ORDER half; the count/desk-grid callers are a separate rewire. **(e)** the cancel-restore still adjusts stock *before* the status write (pre-existing, not introduced here) — if the status write throws, stock is restored and the order is not cancelled. The **ledger stays truthful either way** (it records the movement that physically happened, and the `order_cancelled` event is correctly not written), so this is a transactionality gap, not a ledger gap. **(f)** #56/#59/#60/#61/#62/#63 unchanged.

**THE LEAK, AND WHY THE FIX IS STRUCTURAL.** Yesterday's recon found `DebugPanel` and `RhythmLogger` mounted in `App.tsx` as siblings of `<AppRouter/>` — **outside every auth gate**. The fix was not to add an `isOwner &&`. The panels **moved into `AppLayout`**, which renders only inside `<PrivateRoute>`: **there is now no code path that mounts them for a signed-out visitor.** A conditional can be re-bypassed by the next person who edits it; a mount location cannot be bypassed without deleting the router. The owner-only toggle is then a *second* gate on top. **Neither is load-bearing alone — that is the point.**

**ONE GATE, NOT TWO (§6 r8, the rule this build is an instance of).** `?debug=1` and `?rhythm=1` were the same OPERATION written twice: two `xEnabled()` readers, two sticky localStorage keys, two floating buttons deliberately placed on opposite corners so they wouldn't collide. State is keyed to **(userEmail + role)** and purged when either changes — the old keys were raw localStorage with **no session coupling**, so they survived logout *and* role change, and a device left in debug stayed in debug for whoever signed in next.

**⚠️ THE JUDGEMENT CALL — AND IT CUTS AGAINST EVERYTHING ELSE IN THIS BUILD.** The version stamp is deliberately **NOT** behind the new owner gate, though every other dev surface moved behind it. #141 had put the SHA in the DebugPanel footer — which was correct *then*, and became **wrong the moment this build owner-gated that panel**: a deploy broken enough to break the menu would have **hidden its own tell**, which is precisely the failure tech-debt #60 exists to catch, reintroduced by the build hardening everything around it. So the stamp moved OUT to an always-visible `built <date> · <sha>` line — every screen, every user, outside every gate, `pointer-events:none` so it can never swallow a tap — and was **removed from the panel** (STD-011: one home; two surfaces printing one fact drift, and a drifted version stamp asserts a build you are not running). **A tell must not depend on the thing it is testing.**

**A CAPABILITY DELIBERATELY NOT LOST.** Owner-gating the *viewer* does not stop the *capture*: `installCapture()` still runs in `main.tsx` **before React**, so the pre-login trail — including the customer QR page — is still **recorded**. So `auth.uid()` is NULL for server writes because of where the WRITE runs, not because of how the caller was resolved. Client-direct writes (grid edit, tier dropdown) get the actor free, but **server writes need an app-level event** — which is *why* industry runs both layers. ⚠️ **Mechanism sentence corrected 2026-07-20** (D-50 Layer 1; the original said "→ a service-role client", which is the sentence a future session would design from — same class as tech-debt #61, a note contradicting its own repo). ### 2026-07-17 — THUNDER RECON: THE COUNT RECORD, THE CONFIDENCE PRIMITIVE, AND RECONCILE-TO-SELLABLE (ledger #137): nobody had opened `inventory_counts` — the model was being designed blind. Look-then-decide. The finding: **the pending-capture queue ALREADY EXISTS as rows and NOTHING reads it**; the reconcile "build" is largely a READER + a shared predicate + a grid filter, NOT a new store. REPORT ONLY — zero code, zero schema, zero migration, zero api-fn (12/12)

**Type:** RECON document only — 1 NEW (`docs/decisions/2026-07-17-inventory-reconcile-confidence-recon.md`, the three-lens recon) + this handoff + ledger #137 + DECISIONS-INDEX drift line. **ZERO app code, ZERO schema, ZERO migration, ZERO api-fn (12/12 untouched), ZERO `[TRACE:*]`** — no `.ts`/`.tsx` opened. `npm run verify` NOT run (nothing built). **NO decision number proposed** (per instruction — if David rules an option in, that is where a decision mints). **BENCH: no trigger fires** (no payments/PII/webhooks/AI-calls/invoices/compliance-actions — roster matched, reported per §6 r10). Serves `user_stories.md:362` + `:370` (both `STATUS: written`), cited in the doc.

**WHY IT EXISTED:** two hours of reconcile/confidence design had rested on inference — the table everyone was designing against, `inventory_counts`, had not been opened. Lightning fabricated a trace record the day before and David caught it. This recon is the correction: **look, cite, then decide.** Every claim in the doc carries `file:line`; three claims are labelled BLOCKED (no local service key — same block D-49 hit) rather than guessed.

**THE HEADLINE, AND IT IS A CORRECTION TO THE MODEL:** **the queue is already built — as ROWS — and read by NOTHING.** "Skip & flag" writes `inventory_counts {inventory_id: null, was_unknown: true, item_label, counted_qty, raw_scan}` ([InventoryCount.tsx:545](packages/cultivar-os/src/pages/InventoryCount.tsx#L545)); the typed/ambiguous path writes a labelled row too. But grepping every reader: **there is NO `.from('inventory_counts').select(...)` anywhere** — the migration itself says reconciliation "is DEFERRED — this only leaves room for it." So `inventory_counts` is a **write-only audit log**, and the pending-capture store the design keeps describing **is a table that already has rows in it and no screen.** A large part of "build reconcile" is "build a READER."

**THE SMALLEST VERSION THAT WORKS (David's own question — is it over-designed? Partly yes):**
- **NEED = a shared sellable predicate + a grid filter, no migration.** The refusal that stopped Chinkapin (`sell_price == null || sell_price <= 0`) is **inline and duplicated 3×** ([submit.ts:360](packages/cultivar-os/api/orders/submit.ts#L360), [:914](packages/cultivar-os/api/orders/submit.ts#L914), [CartReview.tsx:131](packages/cultivar-os/src/pages/CartReview.tsx#L131)) with **no shared function** — so showing "not sellable yet" on the grid would fork a **4th copy at the money surface**. Extract it to ONE shared predicate FIRST (the keystone); then a `/inventory` filter over it + "never counted" (derived from the already-written `inventory_counts`) + "still a stub" (`isVarietyStub` already exists). **The reconcile SURFACE is the grid** — `BusinessInventory.tsx` header literally says "board 5.1 reconcile surface"; it needs two derived columns and a filter, not a new screen.
- **ALREADY BUILT, that David may think needs building:** the unknown/pending queue (rows exist, unread), resolve-before-create (built at [InventoryCount.tsx:576](packages/cultivar-os/src/pages/InventoryCount.tsx#L576), `owed`/unproven not missing), the reconcile surface (the grid), and **size-scraping** (`fetchProductVariants` reads Woo variation sizes and writes per-size rows TODAY — the 103 live size-less stubs are **stale data predating the enrichment**, not a missing feature).
- **OVER-designed for today's pain:** `qty_as_of` as a NEW column (currency can be *derived* from the unread table — WANT not NEED); a qty/identity **confidence ladder** (real for the *spoken walk* `:376`, not for the typed/scan path staring at Bur Oak/Chinkapin whose qty is a firm count); **voice** (a separate build with an infra decision in front of it).

**THREE FINDINGS THAT CONSTRAIN ANY BUILD (all cited in the doc):**
- **AC-1 / confidence:** `cost_confidence` is a **DB CHECK** (`20260612_..._cost_confidence.sql:58`), and the 4-value ladder is **5 literal CHECK copies across 3 migrations** + the TS type forked in ≥4 files — **no shared DB domain, no shared primitive** (STD-011). There is **NO identity/qty/tax confidence ladder at all** (`person_spine` has none). So a new `qty_confidence` would become the **6th CHECK copy + AC-1 debt** unless modelled as **growable free-text** (the discovery-JSONB precedent already does exactly that: "NO CHECK — the value-set grows without a migration").
- **E — sizes AND prices are ONE structure, and for LAWNS the price half is empty by nature.** The Woo `data-product_variations` JSON the parser already reads carries `display_price` per variation ([test fixture](packages/shared/src/discovery/catalog-variants.test.ts#L35)) beside the size — parsed and **discarded** ([catalog.ts:451](packages/shared/src/discovery/catalog.ts#L451)). BUT a read-only fetch of the live LAWNS page shows **sizes, no prices** — LAWNS is catalog-only wholesale. So scrape-reads-price is **one JSON key** but **useless for LAWNS**: pricing stays **homework (Lauren enters), not review (Lauren approves)**. That makes O1's "needs price" filter *more* important, not less.
- **F — voice's ceiling-safe path already has a live precedent.** Browser Web Speech API runs in cultivar today ([RhythmLogger.tsx](packages/cultivar-os/src/components/RhythmLogger.tsx), `?rhythm=1`, zero endpoints); the Ignition donor POSTs to an off-repo LAN Whisper. `voice_capture` itself is **not built**, and a server transcriber would be api-fn **#13 = silent deploy failure** (12/12). Voice is a distinct build with an infra decision, not a rider on reconcile.

**THE ORDER (why what before what):** (1) shared sellable predicate FIRST — the keystone; every grid signal depends on it and building it late forks the money rule. (2) grid reader/filter (reads `inventory_counts`, no migration) — unblocks the live pain. (3) `qty_as_of` column only if derived-currency proves insufficient. (4) confidence ladder gated on a **free-text-vs-CHECK decision**, and on the spoken-walk being the active story. (5) voice gated on the 12/12 ceiling call. Does scrape-price shrink the reconcile build? **No — it makes it honestly smaller for LAWNS (sizes recoverable, prices not), which is why "needs price" must be a first-class filter.** Does skip&flag mean the queue exists? **YES, unambiguously.**

**§1.6:** most items **N/A and stated as such** (no code/schema/UI-control/endpoint/money path changed — this is a document). Applicable: **1 STORY** (cites `:362` + `:370`, both written), **10 THREE-LENS** (the doc IS HAVE/NEED/WANT + OPTIONS spanning NEED→WANT, no pre-collapsed recommendation — a recon, per §9 gate 10). **NO built-inventory touch — nothing was built, stated here rather than skipped silently.** **NO owner-prove owed** (a document has no live surface to drive).
